item.title: Abolitionist Architecture: How Black Designers Are Building a Liberatory Future
item.description: The newly appointed president of the National Organization of Minority Architects, Bryan C. Lee Jr., sits down with The KC Defender's Executive Editor Ryan Sorrell to discuss why, in an age of fascism, building a blueprint for liberation means reclaiming the spaces where Black life can flourish The post Abolitionist Architecture: How Black Designers Are Building a Liberatory Future appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: Damning Transcript Exposes Truth Behind Holy Brunch Closure
item.description: What began as a federal RICO lawsuit has become one of Kansas City's most explosive legal sagas. Now, Holy Brunch's owner is blaming Black media for his closure and screenshotting a Black woman reporter in an expletive-laden Facebook diatribe. But court transcripts expose what he knew all along. The post Damning Transcript Exposes Truth Behind Holy Brunch Closure appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: Fear Over Facts: Mizzou’s President Puts Columbia’s Unhoused Residents at the Center of a Public Safety Debate
item.description: University of Missouri President Mun Choi has framed homelessness as a public safety issue following a local student’s killing. But crime data shows no link between homelessness and violent crime. Advocates say that rhetoric has fueled harassment of Columbia’s unhoused community. The post Fear Over Facts: Mizzou’s President Puts Columbia’s Unhoused Residents at the Center of a Public Safety Debate appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: Kansas City Winter Resources for the Unhoused: What to Do and Where to Go When Temperatures Drop
item.description: As winter settles in, hundreds of Kansas Citians are facing the cold without shelter. This guide pulls together shelter, food, medical, and warming resources so people living outside, families navigating homelessness, and those looking to help know where to turn. The post Kansas City Winter Resources for the Unhoused: What to Do and Where to Go When Temperatures Drop appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: Kansas City Passes 5-Year Ban on Mass Detention Facilities
item.description: The move blocks permits for non-municipal detention centers as the Trump regime eyes KC for a 10,000-person ICE concentration camp The post Kansas City Passes 5-Year Ban on Mass Detention Facilities appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: Kansas City at Center of ICE Nationwide Concentration Camp Network
item.description: ICE is eyeing to make Kansas City one of seven "mega centers" in its unprecedented concentration camp network. A local real estate company, Platform Ventures, may "sell out" Kansas City by selling a taxpayer-subsidized warehouse to make it happen. And federal agents are already terrorizing KC residents & going door-to-door. The post Kansas City at Center of ICE Nationwide Concentration Camp Network appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: From Pop-Ups to a Permanent Home: The Outsiders Social Club Reimagines Co-Working in Kansas City
item.description: A new Westport social hub blends coffee, collaboration, and community for Kansas City creatives. The post From Pop-Ups to a Permanent Home: The Outsiders Social Club Reimagines Co-Working in Kansas City appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: SHUT IT DOWN, GET ICE OUT! Nationwide General Strike January 30th
item.description: Following Minnesota's massively successful general strike, unions across the nation are calling for a nationwide general strike this Friday, January 30th. As ICE continues to terrorize our communities, the time to stand up and fight back is here. No politician is going to save us. Only we can save us. The post SHUT IT DOWN, GET ICE OUT! Nationwide General Strike January 30th appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: A Brilliant Boy, a Garbage Dump, and the $415 Standing Between Him and Medical School
item.description: This story marks the first installment in "The Plunder Papers," an ongoing investigative series by two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist Jon Jeter examining why Africans continue to live in grinding poverty seven decades after the alleged close of the colonial era. The post A Brilliant Boy, a Garbage Dump, and the $415 Standing Between Him and Medical School appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.

item.title: KCPD Holds Taxpayers Hostage While Shielding a Killer in Blue
item.description: The department has received $1.2 billion since 2022. Now it claims it can't afford basic services while an officer who has killed three people remains on patrol. A Kansas City Defender investigation. The post KCPD Holds Taxpayers Hostage While Shielding a Killer in Blue appeared first on The Kansas City Defender.
